facts.statement: The genus Ninjatitan contains only one species, Ninjatitan zapatai, which was named and described in 2021 from a partial postcranial skeleton found in 2014.
facts.quote: The genus contains a single species, Ninjatitan zapatai, which was named and described in 2021 based on a partial postcranial skeleton discovered in 2014.

facts.statement: Ninjatitan was an extinct titanosaurian sauropod that lived during the Early Cretaceous (Berriasian to Valanginian ages) in the Bajada Colorada Formation of Argentina.
facts.quote: Ninjatitan (meaning "Ninja giant") is an extinct genus of titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous (Berriasian–Valanginian age) Bajada Colorada Formation of Argentina.

facts.statement: When first named in 2021, Ninjatitan was considered the oldest known titanosaur, but later research suggested the Russian dinosaur Tengrisaurus might be of comparable age and more definitively a titanosaur.
facts.quote: When it was named in 2021, Ninjatitan was identified as the oldest titanosaur known, although subsequent research has cast doubt on this interpretation, as the Russian Tengrisaurus is comparable in age and more conclusively titanosaurian.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest Ninjatitan might be a chimera because its anterior caudal vertebra has features like large lateral pneumatic openings and a specific fossa that are found in rebbachisaurids and diplodocoids rather than in somphospondylans.
facts.quote: Ninjatitan may be a chimera. The anterior caudal vertebra of the holotype bears large lateral pneumatic openings more reminiscent of rebbachisaurids and diplodocines than somphospondylans, and the vertebra bears a deeply excavated prezygapophyseal centrodiapophyseal fossa, a feature only known in diplodocoids.

facts.statement: Conversely, the holotype's dorsal vertebra shows camellate pneumaticity and the scapula has a triangular projection, both features common in titanosauriforms but absent in diplodocoids.
facts.quote: However, the dorsal vertebra of the holotype has camellate skeletal pneumaticity, as in titanosauriforms but not diplodocoids, and the scapula bears a triangular projection not found in any diplodocoid but commonly seen in titanosauriforms.

facts.statement: The Ninjatitan holotype was discovered at the same locality as the diplodocoids Leinkupal and Bajadasaurus, but from a slightly deeper rock layer.
facts.quote: The holotype of Ninjatitan was found at the same locality, but a slightly deeper rock layer, as the holotype of the diplodocoids Leinkupal and Bajadasaurus.

facts.statement: While lacking unanimous features to classify it as a somphospondylan, Ninjatitan possesses traits suggesting it belongs within the Titanosauria clade, either as a basal member or within Colossosauria.
facts.quote: Ninjatitan does not preserve any unanimous features that classify it as a somphospondylan, but it does bear features that suggest it can be included within the clade Titanosauria, either as a basal taxon or possibly within the clade Colossosauria.

facts.statement: In 2025, researchers Averianov and colleagues concluded that Ninjatitan could not be conclusively assigned to Titanosauria because its anterior caudal vertebrae have large pleurocoels similar to the non-titanosaurian Triunfosaurus, suggesting it should be classified outside this clade.
facts.quote: In 2025, Averianov and colleagues reassessed the phylogenetic relationships of Tengrisaurus and other early titanosaurs and allied taxa. They noted that the anterior caudal vertebrae of Ninjatitan have a large pleurocoels, uncharacteristic of titanosaurs but similar to Triunfosaurus, a non-titanosaurian somphospondylan from similarly-aged rock layers in Brazil. As such, the researchers concluded Ninjatitan could not conclusively be assigned to the Titanosauria, and that it should likely be classified outside of this clade.

facts.statement: Ninjatitan zapatai lived approximately 140 million years ago during the Valanginian stage of the Early Cretaceous in what is now South America.
facts.quote: Ninjatitan zapatai es especie conocida del género extinto Ninjatitan de dinosaurio saurópodo titanosauriano que vivió a principios del periodo Cretácico, hace unos 140 millones de años durante el Valanginiense en lo que es hoy Sudamérica.

facts.statement: Ninjatitan reached a length of 20 meters and is known from postcranial remains found in the Bajada Colorada Formation of the North Patagonia, Neuquén Province, Argentina.
facts.quote: Tenía un largo de 20 metros de longitud, encontrada en la formación Bajada Colorada de la Patagonia Norte, Provincia de Neuquén, Argentina, de la cual se conservan restos postcraneales.

facts.statement: The generic name Ninjatitan comes from the nickname of Argentine paleontologist Sebastián Apesteguia, while the specific name zapatai honors technician Rogelio Zapata.
facts.quote: Su nombre genérico proviene del apodo del paleontólogo argentino Sebastián Apesteguia y el nombre específico proviene del técnico Rogelio Zapata.

facts.statement: The presence of a basal titanosaurian sauropod in the Early Cretaceous of Patagonia supports the hypothesis that the group established itself in the Southern Hemisphere and reinforces a Gondwanan origin for Titanosauria.
facts.quote: La presencia de un saurópodo titanosauriano basal en el Cretácico más bajo de la Patagonia apoya la hipótesis de que el grupo se estableció en el hemisferio sur y refuerza la idea de un origen gondwanico para Titanosauria.

facts.statement: Ninjatitan lived between 139.1 and 132.6 million years ago, spanning the Berriasian to Valanginian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Berriasian to Valanginian (139.1 to 132.6 million years ago)
